memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He washed the internal organs and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar." - Lev 9:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The internal organs are washed before they are burned.

We met this detail back in chapter 1. Here it is again, being done for real. The parts nobody would see, caked with the dirt of ordinary life, are cleaned before they go to God.

God cares about the inside.

That is easy to affirm and hard to live. Most of us manage our visible life with considerable care — our speech, our reputation, our public behaviour. The interior gets less attention: what we think about when nobody is talking to us, what we feel when someone else succeeds, what we watch when we are alone.

Jesus was blunt about this with the religious leaders of His day: You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence (Mtt 23:25).

The good news is that God offers to do the washing. David prayed, Create in me a pure heart, O God (Ps 51:10) — create, because he could not manufacture it himself.

You do not have to clean your own interior before bringing it to God. You have to bring it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What part of my inner life have I kept from honest examination?
2. Am I as attentive to my thoughts and motives as I am to my reputation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, wash what no one else can see in me. Create in me a clean heart, because I cannot do it myself. Amen.
